source_text: Quo furore quidem numquam cariturus es, nisi prius obscenum dogma reieceris; quia inter paenitentiae pudorem, numquam tamen a Christianis aversatum, et argumentationis inopiam, graves perferens Symplegadas, necesse est ut bona dicta quibus obrueris, aut sequaris, aut laceres.
pass_a_gloss: From which fury indeed you will never be about to lack, unless first you have thrown off the obscene dogma; because between the shame of repentance, never nevertheless turned away by Christians, and the poverty of argumentation, bearing the heavy Symplegades, it is necessary that you either follow the good sayings by which you are overwhelmed, or tear them.
pass_b_english: You will never be free of that frenzy unless you first reject your obscene doctrine. For you are caught between two crushing rocks: the shame of repentance, which Christians nevertheless never reject, and your lack of an argument. You must either follow or tear apart the sound statements that overwhelm you.

choices.why: Keep Julian's good-of-nature vs good-of-will contrast; do not baptize as 'grace'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
